title: Is LangGraph overkill for a small agent?
snippet: Practitioners compare a three-tool support bot built as a plain loop with the same bot rebuilt as a graph. The consensus: the graph pays off at the second operational requirement, usually resume or approval.

title: LangGraph vs a hand-written loop: the real tradeoff
snippet: A hand-written loop is faster to read and has no dependency. A graph makes state and routing explicit, which helps when several people edit the flow or when a run must be replayed.

title: Checkpointers explained: memory, sqlite, postgres
snippet: MemorySaver is enough for a demo. SqliteSaver covers a single box in development. PostgresSaver is the usual production default because several workers can read the same thread.

title: The cost of one extra LLM call in an agent
snippet: At support volume, one avoidable LLM round trip per ticket is usually more expensive than the infrastructure. Measure the critical path, not the number of nodes: parallel branches can hide latency.

title: Human-in-the-loop without a server
snippet: A checkpoint plus an interrupt lets a graph pause before a side effect and resume from another process. The approval decision should be stored as data, never inferred from the model's prose.
